verdict.rationale: Linear documents team-level visibility controls: private sub-teams can be restricted to parent team members or hidden except to invited members, and initiatives led by private teams are visible only to team members. The Okta material also references existing Linear permissions and admin-managed access, but none of this shows granular roles or per-object edit rights. Missing for 10: documented role definitions (admin/member/guest scopes), granular edit-versus-view permission controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can assign granular permissions and roles to control who can view or edit work

citations.quote: Private to team members — the team is hidden, except to members directly invited to that sub-team
For work that requires tighter access, initiatives led by private teams are only visible to team members.
Linear verifies their identity through Okta and applies their existing Linear permissions. Admins can manage access centrally
